$comment: Expected outcomes for the MDPack conformance corpus. Generated by tools/build-corpus.mjs; do not edit by hand. A Conforming Reader must accept every file under valid/ and reject every file under invalid/, reporting one of the listed error classes.

errorClasses.not-an-mdpack: The file is not an MDPack package: unreadable as ZIP, no manifest, or the manifest does not identify itself as MDPack.
errorClasses.unsupported-version: An MDPack package whose version the reader does not implement. Must be distinguishable from corruption so the user is told to upgrade.
errorClasses.malformed-manifest: mdpack.json is present and identifies itself as MDPack but violates a structural requirement.
errorClasses.integrity-failure: Package contents contradict themselves: checksum mismatch, byte-length mismatch, duplicate entries, truncation, or invalid UTF-8 in a text entry.
errorClasses.security-violation: The package attempts something hostile, such as path traversal or an encrypted entry.
errorClasses.resource-limit: Decompressing the package would exceed a reader resource limit.

valid.description: Manifest and document only, no assets.
valid.notes: The smallest conforming package. Note there is no assets/ directory entry: 0.1 §3.5 requires readers to accept its absence, because ZIP archives do not reliably preserve empty directories.

valid.description: A PNG and a PDF, both referenced by relative path and both declared.
valid.notes: The core happy path: relative reference resolution (§6.2), byte lengths and checksums (§7), and the inline and attachment roles (§4.9).
The mimetype entry is SHOULD for writers and MUST NOT be required by readers (§3.3). A package written with a stock ZIP library will not have one.

valid.description: A manifest carrying nothing but format, version, entrypoint and assets.
valid.notes: Every other member is optional (§4.4). A reader must not require id, title or timestamps, and must fall back to the file name for the display title.

valid.description: Unknown entries and unknown manifest members that must survive a round trip.
valid.notes: Round-trip-preserving Writers (§12.3) must reproduce thumbnails/cover.png, metadata/extra.json, vendor-notes.txt and the com.example.* manifest members unchanged after a read-modify-write cycle. Readers of any class must accept the file. The .scratch/ entry is the one exception: §3.6 says implementation scratch space must neither be extracted nor preserved.

valid.description: A file under assets/ that the manifest does not declare.
valid.notes: Permitted by §4.7. Readers must accept it; a strict validator reports it as untracked, and cleanup tooling lists it as a deletion candidate (§9.3).

valid.description: A Unicode asset name that must be percent-encoded in the Markdown reference.
valid.notes: The document references assets/%D1%81%D1%85%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B0%20%D1%81%D0%B5%D1%82%D0%B8.png, which decodes to "assets/схема сети.png". Exercises step 4 of the resolution algorithm (§6.2) and UTF-8 ZIP entry names (§3.1).

valid.description: References carrying a fragment and a query component.
valid.notes: Both must resolve to assets/appendix.pdf: §6.5 requires the query and fragment to be stripped before matching. A reader that matches the raw string reports a spurious missing asset.

valid.description: An asset declaring a role this specification does not define.
valid.notes: §4.9: readers must ignore unknown role values and must not reject the package. Roles are descriptive metadata, never authorisation.

valid.description: A document referencing only external URLs.
valid.notes: §6.4: external references are not package content. A reader must not fetch them, and in particular must not fetch anything in order to validate the package. Neither reference is a missing asset.

valid.description: document.md prefixed with a UTF-8 byte order mark.
valid.notes: §3.1: writers should omit the BOM but readers must accept and strip one. Note that documentSha256 covers the bytes as stored, including the BOM (§7).

invalid.notes: Must not crash the reader.

invalid.description: A valid package cut off halfway through.
invalid.notes: The central directory is gone. Either classification is acceptable; crashing is not.

invalid.description: A ZIP containing document.md but no mdpack.json.

invalid.notes: §3.4. The package declares an entry document it does not contain.
§4.4. Compared case-sensitively, so an unrelated ZIP that happens to carry an mdpack.json cannot be mistaken for a package.
§4.4. A reader must not assume the current version.
§4.5. Must be reported distinctly from corruption: the user should be told to upgrade, not told their file is broken.
§4.4 and §4.6: entrypoint is required. A reader must not silently assume "document.md".

§4.6: in this version entrypoint must be exactly "document.md", and a reader must never follow it as an arbitrary path. A reader that resolves it against the extraction directory reads a file outside the package.
§4.4: assets is required, even when empty. Unlike most optional members it carries meaning by its absence, so the specification pins it down rather than defaulting it.
A deserialiser that maps this onto a null collection reference will throw when it iterates. The reader must report a clean error instead (§8.9).

invalid.description: assets is an object rather than an array.
invalid.notes: Same hazard as null-assets: the structural shape must be validated before deserialisation results are used.

invalid.description: The manifest declares an asset the package does not contain.
invalid.notes: §4.7. Without this check the document renders with silently broken images.

invalid.description: A declared asset whose path is not under assets/.
invalid.notes: §4.7: a declaration must point under assets/. Permitting arbitrary paths would let a manifest lay claim to mdpack.json or document.md.

invalid.description: Two declared assets sharing an id.
invalid.notes: §4.7: identifiers must be unique within the assets array. A reader keyed by id would silently drop one of them.

invalid.description: A declared asset with no role member.
invalid.notes: §4.7: id, path, mediaType, bytes, sha256 and role are all required of a writer. A declaration missing one of them is not a valid declaration.

invalid.description: A declared asset whose bytes value does not match the stored length.
invalid.notes: §4.7 makes byte-length verification a reader requirement, not just a writer one. This package's sha256 is correct, so a reader that only checks digests accepts it.

invalid.description: A mimetype entry whose contents are wrong.
invalid.notes: §3.3: the entry is optional, but when present it must be correct.

A parent segment at the root of the path. §8.2: an unsafe path invalidates the whole package, not just that entry. The manifest and document here are otherwise perfectly valid, so a reader that only validates paths at extraction time will wrongly accept this file.

An absolute POSIX path. §8.2: an unsafe path invalidates the whole package, not just that entry. The manifest and document here are otherwise perfectly valid, so a reader that only validates paths at extraction time will wrongly accept this file.

A Windows drive letter. §8.2: an unsafe path invalidates the whole package, not just that entry. The manifest and document here are otherwise perfectly valid, so a reader that only validates paths at extraction time will wrongly accept this file.

Parent segments hidden inside an otherwise valid prefix. §8.2: an unsafe path invalidates the whole package, not just that entry. The manifest and document here are otherwise perfectly valid, so a reader that only validates paths at extraction time will wrongly accept this file.

Backslash separators, which some readers normalise too late. §8.2: an unsafe path invalidates the whole package, not just that entry. The manifest and document here are otherwise perfectly valid, so a reader that only validates paths at extraction time will wrongly accept this file.
§8.4. ZIP permits duplicates; extraction overwrites, so the entry a reader validates and the entry that lands on disk can differ.

invalid.description: Two archive entries at assets/pixel.png differing only in case.
invalid.notes: §8.4 requires duplicate detection to be case-insensitive. On Windows and macOS the second entry overwrites the first during extraction, so the bytes a reader verified are not the bytes it later renders.

invalid.description: An asset whose sha256 does not match its bytes.
invalid.notes: §7: asset checksums must be verified before the asset is presented, not only the document's.

invalid.description: The document entry declares an uncompressed size of 8 bytes but expands to far more.
invalid.notes: §8.3. A reader that trusts the declared size reads a truncated document and, without checksum verification, shows the user half a note with no warning. The documentSha256 in this manifest is correct for the full text.

invalid.description: document.md contains a byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8.
invalid.notes: §8.8. Silently substituting U+FFFD turns a detectable error into permanent data damage at the next save.

invalid.description: An asset of 4 MiB of zero bytes, compressing at roughly 1000:1.
invalid.notes: §8.3. Trips the recommended 200:1 compression-ratio limit. A reader with a higher ratio limit may instead reject it on a size limit; either is conforming, but expanding it without bound is not.
